newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

TOP STORIES - Karen renegades and Burmese soldiers have been pushed back across the Salween River from Sob Moei district after a clash with a military-police task force. After the brief exchange of fire yesterday, the renegades and Rangoon troops retreated across the river to a Burmese military camp opposite Ban Sop Moei. The Foreign Ministry will today summon Burmese Ambassador and lodge a strong diplomatic protest against recent attacks on three refugee camps in Thailand by pro-Rangoon guerrillas. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will propose a compromise to defuse the row with the judiciary by giving the judiciary a say in the selection of judges to the supreme administrative court. A source says the prime minister is willing to compromise but will not back down from his position that it is for his government to decide who should be given the charge of the administrative court -- the Justice Ministry, the Council of State, or that it be set up as an independent body. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) decided to upgrade and expand its subcommittee tasked with mapping out the first charter draft, a move that could lend weight to criticism that the CDA had spent too much time soul searching. The expansion of the drafting committee will likely trigger fresh criticism because it could cause new delays and the involvement of ambitious outsiders might put the legitimacy of the CDA at risk. (THE NATION) + + + +

- Unproductive imports are next on the chopping block in an effort to curb spending and reduce the current account deficit. The Council of Economic Ministers has agreed in principle to further steps to slow imports. These would target imports considered to have little productive effect on the economy and export performance, notably luxury consumer goods and expensive cars. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee has flown home empty-handed after a visit to the European Union primarily aimed at restoring trade privileges to Thai shrimp and rice exporters. However, the minister says that Thailand still has hope in further top-level negotiations led by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand has warned commercial banks, finance institutions and credit fonciers to better scrutinise their asset valuers' valuation information and procedures. Because of the rapid growth in demand for asset valuation services, the central bank has urged lenders to exercise careful judgement when external asset valuation information is sought. (THE NATION)
